apply). This file is the *process* trail — what ran, what was decided, what's
next.

## 2026-10-30 (latest): **Autonomous QA round 2 — new angles: authz matrix, fresh install, fault injection, a11y, security, Postgres**

**Status: done. Nothing committed (the owner commits). Tree = `270da487` + yesterday's sweep + this unit.**

**Owner ask:** *"do more rounds like this again and try different angles."*

**Angles (none repeated from 2026-10-29):**
1. **Authorization matrix** — 220 route×method calls as anonymous and as a freshly created non-admin, cross-checked
   against which handlers call `require_admin`: no anonymous leak, no admin-gated handler answering a member; the
   member-reachable "admin-ish" routes (alert prefs, providers, budget settings, stores, nutrition sources) are by design
   (R-038) — budget PATCH by a member noted in FU-964 for confirmation.
2. **Fresh install, driven live** — empty DB on :5172 → `/setup` → first admin → wizard (Skip) → every route on an
   empty household (all empty states render; one copy fix: the empty cookbook said "no recipes match the filters") →
   register a second user → their wizard.
3. **Fault injection** — Playwright route interception failing API reads (1 in 3 with 500 / abort / every read 500)
   across all routes: zero page errors, blank pages or stuck spinners in all three modes.
4. **Accessibility + tap targets** — axe-core WCAG 2.1 AA at 1280 and 375 plus a D-004 measurement with touch
   emulation. Eleven rules fixed to zero (icon-button names, toggle/field names via `SettingsRow` naming its slot
   control, prohibited aria on spans, nav list roles, scroll-region focus, calendar/list roles, progress/slider names,
   44 px settings nav on coarse pointers). Left as FU-963: colour contrast (132 page×width hits, the FU-674 token
   family) and three nested-interactive rows.
5. **Security review** (defensive) — 14 hardening fixes landed (per-username login throttle + timing, change-password
   limit, logo decompression bomb, TTS bounds, push-subscription takeover/https, CORS `*` refused, CSV formula guard,
   client-log cap, LIKE escaping, `web_url` + provider-URL scheme checks, compose secure-cookie default, nginx
   headers); eight contract-level items logged as **FU-964** next to FU-928's SEC-2/3/4 (still owner calls).
6. **Postgres portability + migration drift** — offline DDL emission of the whole chain on the postgresql dialect:
   **eight revisions fail on an empty Postgres** (unquoted mixed-case tables, boolean `= 1`, a VARCHAR(36) FK onto a
   UUID key, constraint names only SQLite ever derived). All fixed in place (SQLite behaviour unchanged for installs
   past them) plus two reflect-first convergence migrations (`e7a2c5f9b3d1` column types, `f4b8d1c6a9e2` constraint
   names); session tz pinned to UTC; `nulls_last`; request-id cap; the schema-drift test now compares names and types.
   **Side finding (FU-965, ⚠️):** SQLite batch rebuilds ran with `foreign_keys=ON`, so earlier parent-table rebuilds
   cascade-deleted child rows — `env.py` now owns the pragma; the owner must check the production DB. **R-102 /
   ADR-099.**
7. **Deep read of the lightly-reviewed areas** (assistant, nutrition, companion seam) — Dora's data-tool questions
   failed on every hosted LLM (no `tool_call_id`, then 60 s "unavailable"); link-status matched products at any store
   (cartesian join on a noload relationship, R-032) so the companion's unsave could delete the wrong product;
   backdated offers overwrote the current price; deal quality compared mismatched units; USDA Atwater energy keys
   dropped foods; probe wrote `verified` onto the saved row; plus confirm/tool-arg 500s. All fixed with tests.
8. **Onboarding / auth / native / print read** — second users re-seeded deleted defaults (HIGH, client fixed; server
   gate FU-960), verify-email bounced to the wizard, native first run probed an empty URL, the theme radio showed
   nothing selected, CSV `\r`, forgot-password rejection; export/print/QR ids now POSTed (the 200-item request-line
   ceiling), folded into one `openHtmlDocumentAsync(path, title, body?)`.
9. **Query budget** — SELECT count + wall time per GET route on the dense seed and on a 2000-item bulk seed: no N+1;
   one real finding, the "print every QR label" sheet at 41 s for 2000 items (FU-961).
10. **Stateful workflow + DB invariants** — create → level → product link → list → tick/price → finish (twice) →
    verdict → substitutes → waste → recipe → cook → plan → move → delete-location; then `foreign_key_check`,
    case-insensitive name uniqueness, canonical substitute pairs, line sequences, entries inside their week, single-recipe
    batches: all hold.

**Gates on the final tree:** pytest **2677 passed** (2605 yesterday; 72 new), vitest **836 / 90 files** (817 → 836),
`vue-tsc` + `npm run lint` clean, `quasar build` green, offline Postgres DDL for the whole chain clean, axe re-audit
0 on the eleven targeted rules, crawl/flows re-driven on the final build.

**Owner-level items (left, logged):** FU-960 (seed endpoint gate; companion contract: offset-carrying `observed_at`,
http(s) `web_url`), FU-961 (QR sheet perf), FU-962 (Android cleartext, native downloads), FU-963 (contrast, nested
rows), FU-964 (security decisions), **FU-965 (check the production DB for cascade-deleted rows)**. Verify section:
`DORA_VERIFY.md` → "Autonomous QA round 2".

**Next up:** owner commits; checks FU-965 first; walks the two verify sections; decides FU-964 (1)+(3) and FU-958.

## 2026-10-29: **Autonomous QA sweep — many angles, ~90 bugs found, ~85 fixed**

**Status: done. Nothing committed (the owner commits). Tree = `270da487` + this unit.**

**Owner ask:** *"I'm going to be away for a long time. Do many rounds of QA from different angles and fix the bugs you
find. Autonomous. Anything that needs my input, leave it. Bugs should be obvious bugs."*

**Angles run (in order):**
1. Baseline gates: pytest 2548 / vitest 796 / build green.
2. Static read-only reviews, parallel (opus): backend ×3 feature slices + the big stock/recipe/list read handlers;
   frontend pages, components, settings pages, composables/helpers; a second round over boot / error handling / PWA /
   Dora intents / shortcuts / sheets.
3. **Frontend↔backend contract audit** (Flask `url_map` dumped and every `services/api/*.ts` call resolved; bodies,
   params and DTOs diffed). This is what caught the two worst regressions — both from `fb49f00a`:
   `bootstrap_admin.py` had lost `hash_password` / `audit_emit` from its imports (every fresh install 500'd on
   `/setup`), and `AxiosHttpClient`'s instance-level JSON content type made axios serialise the chunk-upload
   `FormData` as JSON (every backup restore and spreadsheet import failed on chunk 1).
4. Live, against a dense-seeded throwaway backend on :5171 + the built SPA, with scratchpad Playwright: a crawl of
   all 99 routes at 1440 and 375 (console errors, Vue warns, 4xx/5xx), a phone-width overflow check, scripted user
   flows (login, stock peek, cook mode, recipe edit + leave, lists, planner week nav, reconcile Skip, reports range
   switch, backup upload, import upload, settings toggles, help), and a 522-request API sweep (GET every route with
   real ids; `[]`/`{}`/junk bodies on writes) — zero 5xx before or after.
5. Fix wave: six frontend fix agents + two backend fix agents on **disjoint file sets**, each gated on
   vitest/vue-tsc/lint or targeted pytest; then a **diff-reviewer agent per side**, which found 8 + 7 real follow-on
   defects (one a regression: the new restore dup-key remap would have merged a backup recipe's ingredients into the
   same-named existing recipe, and turned a remapped product link into a PK violation) — all fixed by hand.
6. Playwright smoke (`DORA_E2E_PYTHON=python DORA_E2E_CHANNEL=chrome`): 9 passed.

**What landed** — see `CHANGELOG.md` "Autonomous QA sweep (2026-10-29)" for the user-facing list by surface. The
structural ones: step images survive an edit (new contract: a `step_images` entry is a data URL *or* an existing
image id, server keeps the bytes; `resolve_step_image_entries`); the stock-level optimistic write reverts in place
instead of via the rollback registry (which now has no registrants, FU-952); `/meal-plans` sorts by `start_date`
and the SPA fetches every page (a >50-week household lost weeks and created duplicates); stale-response guards on ~20
keyed loads and a promise queue for planner mutations (**R-101 / ADR-098**); the restore remap limited to reference
parents with join rows re-keyed after decode; trim-to-budget's meal-demand loader keyed off the FK (it had never fired,
R-032); buy-verdict / belief skip unticked lines (R-061); the reconcile queue on a `(scheduled_for, id)` keyset cursor;
the lagged Dora Score comparing like components; template-fork keeping uncooked past days (FU-595 parity).

**Round 2** (boot / PWA / shortcuts / Dora / sheets, after the first wave): eleven more fixes — the Workbox
`dora-api` rule no longer caches the `no-store` health probe (offline banner cleared from cache), `useShortcut` lets
Escape reach a registered shortcut and ignores keys inside menus/dialogs and on buttons, `/` on Stock, the
`?section=` watcher on the item page, the quick-add preset path through `addToList`, catch+toast on the price sheet and
Dismiss all, chunked upload resume-from-`received` with a 5-minute chunk timeout (`RequestOptions` on `post`), the
authed-image blob revoke, and an R-101 guard on the price-history sheet.

**Gates on the final tree:** pytest **2605 passed** (baseline 2548; 57 new), vitest **817 / 87 files** (baseline
796), `vue-tsc` + `npm run lint` clean, `quasar build` green, Playwright smoke 9/9, route crawls clean at both widths,
the scripted flows re-driven on the final build against a fresh seed.

**Left for the owner (logged, not fixed):** FU-952..FU-959 — the finish-dialog count vs. deferred lines and the two
leftover endpoints (a product call), meal-slot rename cascade, swap inside a cook batch, cross-install restore
(stores section / self-FK order), `scanning_enabled` server enforcement, planner queue coverage + stepper busy state,
rollbackRegistry tidy / QR blob revoke / shared test DB path, push-unsubscribe-on-logout + PWA update check.

**Process notes:** every Python text-mode patch (mine and the agents') rewrote LF files as CRLF; a scratchpad
normaliser restored them before the gates — memory note saved. `tests/conftest.py`'s fixed `data/dora.test.db` makes
parallel pytest runs collide (FU-952). The API sweep's `{}` POST to `/onboarding/restart` threw the seeded user back
into the wizard mid-run — reseed between sweeps.

**Verification:** `DORA_VERIFY.md` → "Autonomous QA sweep, browser-verify owed (2026-10-29)" lists the ~16 fixes that
were made from a code read and want one look each; the rest were driven live (listed at the top of that section).

**Next up:** owner commits; walks the verify section; decides FU-958 / FU-957 / FU-956.

## 2026-10-29: **Help area redesigned (20-D4 decided), the drafted guides landed, screenshots captured**

**Status: done. Nothing committed (commit only when asked).**

**Owner ask (2026-10-29):** *"the finalisation plan is complete? I deployed it and don't see any difference to the help
page"* → the help track had been gated on 20-D4 and never shipped. Then: *"redesign the help area completely to look
modern, polished and aesthetic; not verbose; ignore the current layout; take screenshots of the running app yourself for
the guides, crop them, rounded borders."*

**Decision taken (20-D4):** one page per topic (`/help/:group`), a landing with search across every guide, a Common
questions list from the question-shaped titles, and a screenshot slot per guide (the review's own recommendation). The
`/help?q=<title>` deep-link contract the (?) chips and runners use is kept: the landing resolves an exact or unique title
match straight to `/help/<topic>?e=<slug>` and opens that guide.

**What landed**
- **Content:** `web_app/src/help/helpContent.ts` — 14 topics, 166 guides, condensed from `HELP_CONTENT.md`'s 100 drafts
  plus the 28 old entries. Each guide is one summary sentence plus at most one line each for *How*, *Setting* (a real route)
  and *Note*; D-014 voice, D-025 (no em dashes). The old `DoraHelpPage.vue` (hand-maintained tool lists, 13 of 40 stale)
  is deleted; its useful parts are the *Dora* topic (16 guides incl. the faces grid). `/help/dora` still resolves (topic slug).
- **Pages / components:** `HelpPage.vue` (landing: mascot hero, search, topic grid, Common questions, two doors),
  `HelpTopicPage.vue`, `HelpChangelogPage.vue` (`/help/whats-new`; renders the changelog's headings and bullets as text),
  `HelpAboutPage.vue` (`/help/about`; version pill, update note, support copy, Report an issue); `components/help/`
  `HelpShell`, `HelpTopicCard`, `HelpEntryCard`, `HelpShot` (rounded, hairline, card lift), `HelpLegend` (the live
  `StockRowLegend` + the rules dialog), `HelpFaces`. Tokens only; whole-card targets; focus rings; phone layout.
- **Screenshots:** 17 PNGs under `web_app/src/assets/help/` (bundled via `helpImages.ts` glob; a missing file renders no
  figure), captured from the seeded dense household at 1280×2× light Pesto with a scratchpad Playwright script, each
  cropped to the surface (rows, panel, dialog, or the page column). Dora's chat and hint were closed first after the first
  pass bled them into seven shots.
- **Wiring:** routes (`help`, `help/whats-new`, `help/about`, `help/:group`); `doraIntents` "changelog tab" → `/help/whats-new`;
  the food-fact card and the tabs are gone from Help (the endpoint stays for Dora's chat).
- **Tests:** `test/unit/helpContent.spec.ts` ×6 — unique slugs, the five deep-linked titles + the partial "Dora thinks"
  resolve to one guide, every `path`/`setting.path` is a real route, no em dashes / summaries ≤ 45 words, search, every named
  screenshot exists. vitest 796 passed / 83 files; vue-tsc + `npm run lint` clean.
- **Not done (deliberately):** the DoraBot corpus rewrite (11-D1 / FU-946 item 1) — the help corpus now exists as data
  (`HELP_TOPICS`), so an `app_help(topic)` tool can read it; that is FU-946's next step. HelpHint chips on more surfaces
  (the drafts' "Chip:" rows) — the (?) placement sweep is its own unit (FU-951).

**Verification:** driven in the built SPA against the seeded backend on :5171 (Playwright, Chrome): landing, topic with
a deep-linked open guide, `?q=Substitutes` resolving, search, What's new, About, the Dora faces grid, phone width, dark
mode; no console errors. Browser-verify items for the owner in `DORA_VERIFY.md`.

**Next up:** owner walks the Help area once (VERIFY); FU-946's `app_help` tool over `HELP_TOPICS`; FU-951 chip placement.

## 2026-10-23: **Independent QA run — agent 2**

**Status: done, report only. No product code changed.** This is a second independent QA pass, run in
parallel with QA agent 1 and the finalisation session. Deliverable:
`docs/05_investigations/QA_RUN_2_2026-10-23.md`, with 44 numbered findings (9 High, 16 Medium,
15 Low, 4 decisions) plus about 35 static-only leads. Each finding is tagged LIVE / CODE / STATIC. The
report includes a **de-duplication table against QA1's report**.

**What ran.** Everything ran from a detached worktree at `%TEMP%\qa2wt`, because the shared
`web_app/dist` was being rebuilt by another session mid-run.
- **Gates:** pytest 2430 passed, 1 failed (a Hypothesis `too_slow` flake under load, QA2-40); vitest
  747/66; vue-tsc and eslint clean; spa build ok.
- **Browser sweep:** a Playwright crawl of 75 routes at desktop and phone width, plus interactive flows.
- **API probes:** all 304 routes, 768 calls: real, random and junk ids, and empty, malformed and
  wrong-type bodies. That produced 0 × 5xx; the 5xx in QA2-11 needed specific payload shapes.
- **Other probes:** a member privilege probe, delete-cascade checks, and a migrations-from-empty fresh
  install walked through setup and onboarding.
- **Static sub-audits:** four read-only agents covered auth, money, units and dates.

**Headline findings only QA2 has.**
- QA2-05: the stock-value report is inverted; it skips sequence 0 = Stocked.
- QA2-06: trim-to-budget's meal-demand loader reads a `noload` relationship, so it never sees meals.
- QA2-08: the expiry icon parses dates as UTC and turns red at 10:00 on the expiry day.
- QA2-09: the CSP has no `media-src`, so `blob:` server-voice audio can't play. This extends FU-853.
- QA2-10: plaintext passwords in the debug request log (live).
- QA2-12: a fresh install defaults the timezone to UTC, so server "today" lags a day in AU mornings (live).
- QA2-21: the SPA's default API base is `:5170` even when the app is served single-origin.

**Shared with QA1, now also confirmed live by QA2:** stored XSS via image mimetype, open
self-registration, reset-link `Origin` poisoning (the dry-run email carried an evil-host link), and
password change not revoking other sessions.

**Ledgers.**
- **FU-928:** an umbrella FU pointing at the report, not 44 separate FUs, to avoid id collisions with
  the concurrent sessions. The fixer should split it as items are picked up.
- **Not touched:** `DORA_VERIFY.md` (no new verify items). `PROJECT_STATE.md` was left to the
  finalisation session, which is editing it right now. Add QA2's High items under Needs-attention at
  its next regeneration.

**Close-gate.**
- **R-rules:** no code touched.
- **ADR evaluation:** no new rule. Candidates for the fixer: "household-local date helper is the only
  way to turn a UTC timestamp into a date" (QA2-12/13/25, R-021) and "every icon-only `BaseButton`
  needs an `aria-label`" (QA2-28).

**Next up:** the fixing agent works through QA1 and QA2 together using the overlap table. Start with
SEC-1/QA2-01, QA2-03, QA2-04, then QA2-05/06/07.

- SEC-3: open self-registration gives immediate access to all household data.
- QA1-5: re-finishing a done list restocks its items again.
- SL-3 / SL-8: a finished list can be cleared, added to, or reopened to draft.
- AD-1: invalid `nutrition_mode` returns 500.
- S-9: linking an already-linked product returns 500.
- RC-3: negative recipe servings are accepted.
- SEC-7: anonymous client-log writes are unbounded.
- QA1-1: unauthenticated `/health` exposes the budget.

Plus about 70 traced-in-code findings across every surface. All are listed with IDs, files and repros.

- **Ledgers not updated:** findings are not yet in `DORA_FOLLOWUPS.md` or `DORA_VERIFY.md`. I left them alone to avoid colliding with the concurrent finalisation session. The fixing agent should triage the report into FUs.

known FU-762 buy-verdict reds (the 5 `test_email_sender` errors in the full run
were my `-p no:logging` flag starving `caplog`; 16/16 pass without it). vitest
**749 / 66**, `vue-tsc` clean, `eslint` clean on every touched file. Six new e2e
tests in `test_shopping_line_defaults.py`; `shoppingListRailItem.spec.ts`
rewritten to the new row. Driven on 5171/5174 at 375 (Pixel 5, touch) and 1440.

**Decisions worth reviewing.**
- **Picked offers price the line again, reversing half of 09-17.** The owner
  asked that picking an offer "override the price shown" and un-picking restore
  it. Ladder is now actual → **picked** offer → historic → none. The
  cheapest-offer fallback still prices nothing, and nothing records spend until
  a price is entered in shop mode, so the 09-17 spend rule holds. Picking an
  offer also writes the offer's store to `planned_store_id` server-side;
  un-picking leaves the store.
- **Offers vs preferred buys follow `features.products`**, the same gate the
  stock page uses: products on → the name dropdown lists offers; off →
  preferred buys. Never both.
- **`_line_defaults.apply_line_defaults`** is now the single place a new line's
  planned store / preferred buy / picked offer are decided (add-line,
  quick-add, auto-generate, low-stock trigger). Memory = the item's most recent
  earlier line, so a cleared choice stays cleared. Side effect: quick-add now
  prefills the usual store, which it never did. Identity-map trap hit on the
  way (the handler's earlier `by_id` left `StockItem.products` noload-empty,
  FU-872's shape); avoided by relying on the unlink handler's invariant that a
  line's `selected_product_id` is always a linked product.
- **Quantity floor is 1** on client and server (`ge=1` on add + update).
- **Keyboard:** `interactive-widget=resizes-content` (Android) plus
  `boot/keyboardInset.ts` publishing `--vv-inset-*` from `visualViewport`, with
  `app.scss` offsetting `.q-dialog__inner` (iOS). App-wide, covers raw
  `q-dialog`s too. Not testable headless, so it is in DORA_VERIFY.
- **Kept:** "You saved" on the receipt and "Trip total" mid-shop (owner only
  flagged the draft's "Saving"). The run and receipt cards use the same
  figure layout as the draft.

**Answers owed to the owner (in the reply, not in code):** the price sheet is
"Price each": the shelf ticket's big number for one item, not per 100g (label
fixed 09-17); custom products exist (09-08); preferred buys are the no-products
stand-in, so yes, mutually exclusive, and now the list agrees.

**Verified and deleted from DORA_VERIFY:** "The burger sits right" (09-19):
seen at 1440 (mark beside name, verdict at the far end) and 375 (mark beside
name, verdict under the quantity), no collision with the chevron.

**Known trade-off:** on a phone the name gets ~141px on line one because the
price spans the reorder+delete tracks; long offer names truncate. Fine by the
owner's sketch; revisit if he flags it.

**ADR evaluation:** no new rule. "An invisible control must be `display:none`,
not `opacity:0`" is a candidate if it recurs a second time.

**Next up:** nothing blocking; DORA_VERIFY "2026-09-27 phone pass" is the
outstanding browser work.

## 2026-09-19 — **Line provenance: seven values become one boolean**

**Status: built and green; browser-pass owed.** pytest **2379 passed** with only
the four known FU-762 buy-verdict reds, vitest **749 / 66 files**, `vue-tsc`
clean, `eslint` clean on every touched file. `test_migrations` green — single
head, upgrade-from-empty clean. Not yet driven live; four checks parked in
`DORA_VERIFY.md` under "Shopping lists — the auto-added mark (2026-09-19)".

**What the owner asked for.** The conversation started as a design question —
"what are the sources, and what are better ways to show auto-added items?" — and
converged on deleting the question instead. The reasoning, in his words:
auto-generate *is* the path where you asked for a whole list, so stamping each
row with which source produced it tells you what you just typed into the dialog.
The only distinction worth a visual is **"nothing the user did put this here"**,
which is exactly one writer: the low-stock trigger in `update_stock_item`.
He then rejected keeping a one-value enum "just because that was the original
code shape", and asked for the retired "flagged" and "primary list" vocabulary
to be obliterated wherever it still appeared.

**Done.**
- `ShoppingListLine.added_via` (str, 7 values) → `is_auto_added` (bool).
  Migration `a1c7e4b9d2f6`. Historical rows collapse to False — `auto_low_stock`
  was written by *both* machines and nothing on the row distinguishes them, so a
  faithful backfill isn't possible; pre-release, a wrong mark is worse than none.
- `PROVENANCE_PRIORITY` / `_PRIORITY_INDEX` / `_Candidate` / `_Candidate.detail`
  deleted from `auto_generate.py`. Dedupe is now `setdefault`.
  `test_auto_generate_priority.py` deleted with the ladder it tested.
- `sources.flagged` → `sources.essentials`. It always queried `is_essential`;
  there has never been a flag column. Dialog copy fixed to match.
- **The wand → the burger** on `ShoppingListPlanRow`, on `is_auto_added` lines
  only, with the verdict chip pushed right. Closes half of FU-864 (which is
  narrowed to `DraftShopCard` alone); the wand correctly keeps the AI-mode
  marker, and a stock-level rule involves no model.
- **"primary list" swept.** The stored flag died in P6-01 but the vocabulary
  outlived it: `primary_target_resolver.py` → `quick_add_target_resolver.py`,
  `resolve_primary_target` → `resolve_quick_add_target`, the route
  `/shopping-lists/primary/lines` → `/quick-add/lines`, SPA `isPrimary` →
  `isQuickAddTarget`, and — the real bug — Dora's own copy told the user to
  *"Set one as primary so I know where to drop new additions"*, a feature that
  no longer exists. Also removed: a module docstring advertising
  `POST /append-low-stock-essentials`, an endpoint with no route and no caller.

**The judgement call worth reviewing.** `trim_to_budget` scored three of its
five tiers off `added_via`, which I only found because an earlier grep truncated
at 20 lines — worth remembering. Two substituted cleanly and read *better*:
tier 2 now uses the item's live stock band, tier 5 the meal-demand map, both of
which answer the tier's actual question instead of trusting a label frozen weeks
earlier. Tier 1 ("habit — can wait") had no other signal, so rather than delete a
working feature I extracted `_frequently_added.py` — one ranking query now shared
with `auto_generate`, where it had been duplicated (R-003).

**This changed behaviour, deliberately:** tier 5 used to require the line be
stamped `auto_recipe`/`auto_meal_plan`, so a hand-added line for a meal five days
out was never offered as a trim even though it's just as deferrable. It is now.
`test_tier1_not_applied_when_meal_booked_soon` was asserting `out == []` and now
pins tier 5 with the reason string; the new comment records why.

**Next up:** nothing blocking. The browser-pass in `DORA_VERIFY.md` is the only
outstanding work on this. FU-913 (the two overlapping essentials sources in the
New list dialog) is the natural follow-on if he wants the source picker tidied.

## 2026-09-17 (later) — **Shopping lists: a 24-item owner pass, and the collapse snap that wasn't a curve**

**Status: built, gated, AND driven live.** pytest **2389 passed** with only the
four known FU-762 buy-verdict reds, vitest **749 / 66 files**, `vue-tsc`,
`eslint src/`, `quasar build` clean. Driven on the isolated 5171/5174 pair at
**1440 and 375**. Three tests added (back-to-draft ×2, the offer/spend rule),
three updated to the new contracts.

**The headline is a three-line CSS fix with an app-wide reach.** The owner has
reported the same thing at least three times: *"there's a snap at the end which
looks ugly and not smooth (when collapsing). This keeps recurring."* Sampled
frame by frame rather than re-tuned by feel: the card eases **199px → 29px over
~250ms, holds, then drops 29 → 0 in one frame**. 29px is the body's own
`padding: 12px/16px` + its 1px border — `q-slide-transition` animates `height`,
and height cannot go below the padding box, so the last 29px were never animated
at all. They vanished when `v-show` set `display: none`. Every disclosure whose
*caller* had padded the body did this, which is exactly why it kept coming back.
The animated box is now bare and the padding sits on a new
`.collapsible-card__inner` (**R-091 / ADR-088**). Re-measured: 199 → 165 → … → 3
→ 2 → 1 → 0.

**The offers decision went further than my options offered, and the owner was
right.** I asked whether to stop offers pricing lines in planning only or
everywhere; he picked everywhere, and added the mechanism: *"force the user to
enter a price, and there's the option of selecting an offer to fill the price in
shop mode via the price modal."* He had also spotted the bug underneath it —
clicking an offer chip does nothing to the price, because the estimate ladder
puts purchase history **above** offers, so committing to an offer changed
nothing visible on any line he had ever bought. So: the offer rung left the
ladder, the tick-time and finish-time snapshots are gone, and the price sheet
grew a **Seen at** chip that fills the price (and its store) when tapped.
Consequence he accepted up front: a list you never price records no spend.

**That broke five Reports tests, which was the point of running them.** Two
surfaces degraded correctly on their own — spend-by-store and usage stats
already coalesce `actual_unit_price` with the snapshot and count unpriced ticked
lines as coverage rather than dropping them. The **savings-captured** report did
not: it filtered on `picked_offer_price IS NOT NULL`, so it would have gone
permanently empty. Rather than let a whole card die quietly, finishing still
freezes the offer's **RRP** (`list_price_at_pick`) on lines that carry a price
the user entered — context for their number, not a substitute for it — and the
report measures against `actual_unit_price`. Savings now mean something
stronger than before: measured against what you actually paid. `_spend_seeding`
was updated so a seeded "purchase" records a price the way a real one does, and
a new test pins the rule that an offer alone records no spend (a silent, and
flatteringly *larger*, failure mode).

**Two defects I introduced and caught in the live pass**, both worth recording
because both looked fine in the diff: the caret's absolute-positioning rule
targeted `.sl-overview > .collapsible-card__caret` when the caret is a child of
the *header*, so it stopped being positioned at all and fell to the bottom-left
of the band; and turning the run face's `v-else-if` chain into two `v-if`s
orphaned the final `v-else`, which put **Put away** on drafts.

**The rest, briefly.** The summary card's caret stopped taking a column (it was
shortening every full-width block in the header by 44px while the rows below ran
full width). *Order by* → **Group by**, and `manual` → `none` through the type,
the labels, the persisted preference and the specs — every other mode names what
you're grouped by, so "Manual" named the mechanism. A receipt lost its
duplicated `$X Spent` headline, its rename pencil, and the standalone "Where you
spent it" card that made the panel jump position when a list finished. The row
name became the preferred-buy picker (retiring "Buy hint", a control whose name
nobody could decode) and stopped linking to the stock item; the provenance
captions under the price and on the caption line went. The store picker's empty
option is always **Any store** — it used to render "<resolved store> (default)",
which is the whole reason "any" and "usual" read as one setting — with the usual
store marked `(usual)` in the menu only, and prefilled onto new lines
server-side so the row shows a real choice. Add-to-list lost its second step,
its stars and its explainer, and keeps frequent-first ordering *under a filter*,
which it previously abandoned the moment you typed. The price sheet says **Price
each** (it was never a measurement unit — the value is the price of one, and the
log-price form differs because an observation genuinely needs a measure) and
prints the line total. Rail rows wear the status pill's three glyphs, a quiet
"next up", and one count grammar. **Back to draft** is new, with a server
endpoint that unticks everything and refuses a finished list.

**Not verified (in `DORA_VERIFY.md`):** the name-dropdown and Seen-at chips on a
real coarse-pointer phone, and the new flush/receipt card in the dark themes.

**Next up:** owner walks the verify items. **FU-780** (this page is still 3,000+
lines, R-001) is now the obvious next unit — two batches have landed on it and
the surface is as fresh as it will get.

**Open questions for user:** none blocking. One thing worth his eye: with offers
no longer pricing anything, a products install's *planning* totals will read
lower and the "N items with no price yet" count higher until prices are entered
— by design, but it is a visible change in the numbers.

## 2026-09-17 — **Shopping lists: a nine-item owner UI batch (overlaps, card-in-card, receipt polish)**

**Status: built, gated, AND driven live.** pytest **2386 passed** with only the
four known FU-762 buy-verdict reds (unchanged, still not ours), vitest **749 /
66 files**, `vue-tsc`, `eslint src/`, `quasar build` clean. Driven on the
isolated 5171/5174 pair (`data/scratch-verify.db`, money + products on; the
owner's :5170 was never started) at **1440 and 375**. No new components; the
plan row lost one wrapper.

**The owner's report was "too many minor points to write down — look yourself",
with eleven bullets attached.** Three of them turned out to be the same defect.

**1. The action cell was smaller than its contents, and had been all along.**
`--sl-act-w: 104px` held three 36px icon buttons and two 4px gaps — 116px.
Measured before touching anything: on *Full Cream Milk* at 1440px the **Move up
arrow rendered at x=968 against a cell starting at x=980**, i.e. 12px outside
its own column, printing on the money. Invisible on a desktop only because
reveal-on-approach keeps those buttons at `opacity: 0`. A phone has no hover and
`BaseButton` gives it the D-004 44px floor, which takes the same cell to 140px
in a 76px track — so *"in draft mode on mobile, price is on top of the reorder
controls"* was the desktop bug, twice as bad, on the one surface that couldn't
mask it. Widths are now arithmetic over `--sl-act-btn`, which the coarse-pointer
query redefines (**R-090 / ADR-087**).

**2. `grid-row: 1 / -1` does not mean "span every row".** Negative line numbers
resolve against the *explicit* grid; this grid declares no `grid-template-rows`,
so all rows are implicit, the explicit grid is one line long, and the
declaration collapses to a single row — pinning row 1 to the 44px quantity tile
and adding **18px of dead air above every caption**. That is the other half of
*"buttons looking too small for the elements around them ... something is up"*:
the rows were tall for a reason that had nothing to do with their contents.
`span 3` fixes it; desktop rows went 134px → 102/104px with the overlap gone and
the money column finally landing on one x (it was drifting 850/869 by row,
because the track was `auto`).

**3. The phone row is two lines now, and the wrapper had to go.** At 375px the
name cell measured **123px holding 219px of content** — `q-btn`-based store and
buy-hint menus don't shrink — so the caption ran straight across the price.
`.sl-row__main` was a box holding three stacked children inside *one* grid cell,
and a wrapper can't hand its children to a different column, so the row is flat
and every cell is placed explicitly (the shape `ShoppingListReceiptRow` already
used). Line one is quantity + name + delete; price, caption and offers go below
across the full width, reorder rides the caption's line. Captions truncate
instead of wrapping to three lines, offers scroll sideways, and the ± stepper
now *widens* the row rather than floating over the item's name and off the left
edge — a reflow you asked for is not the class of motion bug that float
prevented (hover, which a phone doesn't have). Rows: 149/185px → 139/152px, and
nothing overlaps at either width.

**4. The card-in-card was a selector leak.** `StoreSpendCard` is itself a
`CollapsibleCard`, and the overview card styled `:deep(.collapsible-card__header)`
— *any* header underneath — so the hero gradient band and its padding were being
painted a second time inside its own body. Direct-child selectors, plus a
`flush` variant (no border, no radius, no surface, caption-sized heading), and it
reads as a region of the card it sits in. Its key also gained a swatch for **No
store set**, which had none: the hatch moved out of `ProportionBar`'s scoped
block into `.dora-fill-unassigned` so the pip and the segment it labels cannot
drift (Reports' own no-store bucket can adopt it — FU-843).

**5. The page flash was a one-line fix with a comment already describing it.**
Closing the quick-add sheet called `load()`, which nulls `detail` so a
*navigation* shows a skeleton — the page has had `refreshAllQuietly()` since
August, written when picking a shop day did exactly this, and the fix never
reached the sheet beside it.

**6. "Refresh deals" is gone, and the owner's instinct was right.** He asked why
it wasn't automatic; it turns out it was never a refresh. The handler only
cleared `selected_product_id` values whose product was no longer linked, and the
detail read already resolves each line's offer from the *currently linked*
products and falls back to cheapest — so an active list was always showing
current deals and the button changed nothing visible, while its name promised a
scrape. Endpoint, handler, client method, type and toolbar button deleted
(pre-release, no shim); the bookkeeping moved into
`unlink_product_from_stock_item`, where the fact actually changes, which also
stops a selection reviving if the same product is linked again later.

**7. FU-769 reproduced, and the August hypothesis was wrong.** It was filed as a
suspected *refresh* gap. Driven live: the store never reached the server at all
(`purchased_store_name: null` after a hard reload). `savePriceEditor`
short-circuits on a blank price into `clearPriceOverride`, which clears the price
**and** the store — so "Bought from" only saved if you also typed a price. Split
into two decisions (`saveStoreOnly`); verified Baby Spinach moving Woolworths →
Aldi with no reload. **FU-805** was closed in passing while rebuilding that row:
"estimated, no price entered" now reads "estimated from your last receipt".

**Also:** the overview card lost ~40% of its padding (225px → slimmer at 1440,
~390px on a phone) and its control row stops drawing a divider across 900px of
empty space on the receipt face; the phone list picker moved **above** the
toolbar (the toolbar acts on *this* list) and became one bordered field with the
pencil as a segment; the receipt dropped its row dividers (it was using leaders
*and* rules — the leader is the device) and gained document margins; the
deferred-to-budget reason left its `q-chip`, which cannot wrap, and so had been
printing under the "Add back" button; `PriceEntryPrefillDto` gained
`observed_at`, so the log-price dialog says *when* ("Prefilled from your last
receipt · 17/09/2026") and is titled with the item's name alone.

**Tests:** two added, both pinning server contracts a client can't re-derive —
`observed_at` on the prefill, and the unlink-clears-selection cleanup (invisible
by design, so a regression would be silent). One vitest updated for the hatch
class rename. No Playwright specs added, per the stance.

**Not verified (in `DORA_VERIFY.md`):** a real coarse-pointer phone, the armed
stepper's reflow on touch, and the flush store card + hatched pip in the two
dark themes.

**Next up:** owner walks the three verify items. **FU-780** (`ShoppingListDetail.vue`
is 3,000+ lines, R-001) was deliberately *not* folded in — it would have doubled
this diff and made the visual changes unreviewable — but the surface is fresh now
and it is the obvious next unit on this page.

**Open questions for user:** none blocking.

## 2026-09-13 — **Cook mode: four-item owner batch (notes band, step highlight, numerals, gaps)**

**Status: built, gated, AND driven live.** vitest **749 / 66 files**, `vue-tsc`,
`eslint src/`, `quasar build` clean; pytest untouched (no server change). Driven
on the isolated 5172/5175 pair at **1280 and 375**, on *Sunday Ragu* (the seed's
only structured recipe — 16 steps, 2 sections, 3 tools). New:
`components/recipes/CookNotesSection.vue`.

**1. "Your notes" is a band on the step card, collapsed.** Owner: *"Make 'your
notes' an extension visually of the step text area. Possibly collapsed?"* It was
a bordered card below the Prev/Repeat/Next row — a fourth widget between the step
and the three section panels. The step card already had the idiom: the timer is a
sunken band hanging off its bottom. The notes are a second one, after the timer
(the timer is about *this* step, the notes about the recipe, so the step-specific
thing stays nearest the step). **Collapsed by default** is the substantive half —
notes don't change as you step, so an open one pushes the step text further down
the screen on every single step; the header stays visible so you know they exist,
and the open state persists across steps because the component never unmounts.
Verified: `notesInsideStepCard: true`, flush with the card's bottom edge (1px =
the card border), header 47px (clears D-004 on coarse pointers).

Extracted rather than inlined because **image mode has no step card** — that call
site wraps the same component in its own `q-card`. One implementation, two hosts.

**2. The All-steps current row matches the ingredient/tool highlight.** Owner:
*"Match highlight styling for current step from the all steps area with the
ingredients and tools highlight. Prefer ingredients and tools highlight look."*
It was Quasar's `:active`, which only recolours text. Now `.cook-row--highlighted`
— measured identical to an ingredient row: `bg rgb(228,237,251)`, `border-left
3px rgb(37,147,92)`. **`aria-current="step"`** carries what `active` used to
imply. Deliberately *not* borrowed: `.cook-row--dim`. On ingredients the dimming
answers "which of these does this step need?", so the rest are noise; in All steps
every other row is something you read ahead to, so dimming them would dim the
list's purpose.

**3. Step numerals are the recipe view's circles.** Owner: *"Use same number
circles styling as on the recipe view."* The chrome already lived in the shared
`css/recipeSteps.scss` (its own header says it was extracted there for exactly
this reason, R-001); cook mode was the last numbered step list still drawing its
own. Measured byte-identical to the recipe view: `34px / 50% / rgb(222,247,235) /
rgb(37,147,92) / 700`. `.cook-row__avatar` went 32px → 34px so the column holds
the circle without squashing it — which keeps the deliberate alignment of
quantity, tool glyph and step number at one x.

**One shared-file change:** `.dora-steps__num` now reads
`var(--dora-step-num, 34px)`. The variable is declared on `.dora-steps`, and cook
mode uses the numeral alone inside a `q-item` with no such ancestor — without the
fallback both dimensions resolve to `auto` and the circle collapses. Consumers
wanting a different size still declare the variable on an ancestor and win.

**4. Gaps between the three sections.** `margin-bottom: var(--space-4)` on
`.cook-section`; measured 16px / 16px. They were flush, so three panels with a
deliberately *shared* shape (the 09-01 pass) read as one striped block — the
shared shape was working against itself.

**Decisions made:**
- Notes default **collapsed**, not open — the owner asked it as a question
  ("Possibly collapsed?"). One-line reversal if it reads wrong in a real cook.
- The notes band went *after* the timer band, not before.
- The highlight took the ingredient look wholesale but not the dimming (above).

**Files touched:** `components/recipes/CookNotesSection.vue` (new),
`pages/RecipeCookMode.vue`, `css/recipeSteps.scss`, `CHANGELOG.md`.

**Standards close-gate:** R-001 (the notes panel is one component across two
hosts; the numeral circle is the shared class rather than a third copy),
R-002 (no raw colour — all four changes are tokens), R-003 (the numeral chrome
keeps its single source), D-004 (the one new control clears 44px on coarse
pointers). No new rule warranted: every decision here is an application of
existing ones. No unexplained violations.

**Next up:** nothing owed from this batch. Standing queue unchanged — the
meal-planner browser pass is still the largest verify debt.

**Open questions for user:** the highlight you asked to standardise on is a
**blue** fill (`--semantic-info-soft`) with a **green** accent rule
(`--brand-primary`). That's pre-existing and now on three surfaces rather than
two, so it's more visible than it was. Say if you want the fill on the brand axis
to match its rule.

## 2026-09-13 — **Three-item owner batch: tooltip dwell, the blank toast, shelf-price denominators**

**Status: built, gated, AND driven live.** pytest **2384 passed** (the four known
FU-762 reds only), vitest **749 / 66 files**, `vue-tsc` and `eslint src/` clean.
Verified by driving the running app on the isolated 5172/5175 pair against the
dense seed — all three items confirmed with observed values, not inference.
New: `web_app/src/helpers/unitPriceDisplay.ts` + its spec. **R-089 / ADR-086**
established; **R-088 amended**.

**1. Info (?) chips open instantly again.** Owner: *"recent feedback to increase
time before tooltips appear for mobile … has been applied too broadly. For info
(?) chips specifically, I'd expect those to be instant."* R-088/ADR-085's
`BaseTooltip` 500 ms dwell is right for its stated reason — a tap on a *button*
shouldn't flash the label on the way to doing the button's job — and wrong for a
control whose only job is the tip. `InfoTip` sets `:delay="0"`, in the shared
component, so it stays one decision in one place. While there, the four (?)
chips that were still hand-rolled `q-icon` + `BaseTooltip` (Alerts, Stocktake,
Cookbook's *Cookable now*, Price history ×2) moved onto `InfoTip` — R-001, and
they'd otherwise have kept the 500 ms and the wrong size. **Measured live: 18 ms
to the tip.**

**2. The blank blue info toast.** Owner: *"I saw a blank blue info toast when I
was offline reconnecting. What was that? Fix?"* It was
`useNetworkStatus.onBrowserOnline`'s *"Network detected. Checking the server…"*,
and it was blank because **every info toast in the app has been drawing its
message in white on `--surface-elevated`** since the B7/D-002 change made `info`
the neutral kind. Quasar seeds every notification with `textColor: 'white'`
before any registered type is applied and emits it as `text-white`, which its own
stylesheet declares `!important` — so `.dora-toast--info`'s `color` never won.
Light themes only (dark ones have a dark elevated surface), which is why 24-odd
call sites survived it. What was left visible was the icon, the left spine and
the progress bar, all `--semantic-info`: "blank blue". Fixed in `app.scss` with
`!important` on the ink — the alternative, suppressing the seed from the
registration, needs `textColor: undefined`, which `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`
rejects without a cast. **Verified live**: class `text-white` is present on the
element exactly as diagnosed, computed ink is now `rgb(22,39,36)` on
`rgb(245,250,249)`.

Also corrected in the same file: **three offline toasts still promised a write
queue that was removed on 2026-08-23.** `OfflineBanner`'s copy was fixed at the
time and the toasts were missed, so reconnecting said *"Syncing any queued
changes"* when offline is read-only. All three now match the banner's line.

**3. Prices quoted the way shelves quote them.** Owner: *"Log price and possibly
other areas I can't recall — shouldn't be displaying in such low amounts e.g.
'≈ $0.01 per g'. Stores always show per 100g, or per 100ml."* The convention
already existed and was already right — `units.display_denominator_for`, read by
four server-rendered surfaces. The two the owner was looking at couldn't reach
it, because both quote a price the server has never seen: `PriceEntry` previews
while you type, and `RecipeCostDialog` gets the price in the linked product's raw
`size_unit`. Both had grown a private answer. Rather than a third one, the Python
rule became a **data table** (`PRICE_DISPLAY_RULES`) with the existing function
as a thin read over it, emitted into `units_table.ts` by `scripts/dump_units.py`,
with `helpers/unitPriceDisplay.ts` as the client reader — the same mechanism the
unit table itself uses, now written down as **R-089**. `display_denominator_for`'s
behaviour is unchanged, checked across both conventions and both flip boundaries.

Measured in the running app: entry preview `$3.50 / 500 g` → **≈ $0.70 per 100g**
(was ≈ $0.01 per g), `$6.90 / 1 kg` → **$6.90 per kg**, `$8.75 / 500 ml` →
**$1.75 per 100ml**, `$4 / 2 L` → **$2.00 per L**. Cost breakdown, against 27
real seed lines: Spaghetti **$0.00 / g → $0.30 / 100g**, Greek Yoghurt
**$0.01 / g → $0.74 / 100g**, and every line already quoted per kg / L / ea
untouched. Note this *also* moves the cost dialog off its old "/kg below $0.05"
answer and onto /100g, which is the owner's stated expectation and what the rest
of the app now shows for the same product.

**Decisions made:**
- A `Base*` wrapper default is a default, not a ban on the prop — overriding it
  **in another shared component**, with a reason, is compliant. Written into
  R-088 as an amendment so the next session doesn't "fix" `InfoTip` back.
- The cost dialog was *not* fixed server-side (adding display fields to the DTO),
  even though that's the R-003-purest option for that one surface. It does
  nothing for the price-entry preview, which is the surface actually reported, so
  the client would have needed the rule anyway.
- The offline toast copy was in scope: the owner asked *"what was that?"* about a
  reconnect toast, and what it says is wrong.

**Files touched:** `dora_api/domain/units.py`, `scripts/dump_units.py`,
`web_app/src/generated/units_table.ts` (regenerated),
`web_app/src/helpers/unitPriceDisplay.ts` + `test/unit/unitPriceDisplay.spec.ts`
(new), `components/dora/PriceEntry.vue`, `components/recipes/RecipeCostDialog.vue`,
`components/help/InfoTip.vue`, `boot/notifyTypeRegistration.ts`, `css/app.scss`,
`composables/useNetworkStatus.ts`, `pages/AlertsPage.vue`,
`pages/StocktakeRunner.vue`, `pages/RecipesOverview.vue`,
`pages/PriceHistoryPage.vue`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `ENGINEERING_STANDARDS.md`.

**Standards close-gate:** R-001 (four hand-rolled (?) chips folded into
`InfoTip`; two private denominator rules folded into one reader), R-003 / **R-089**
(the convention stays server-owned and is mirrored, not retyped), R-088 (amended,
not violated). No unexplained violations. One new rule + ADR.

**Open questions for user:** the cost breakdown now says `/100g` where it used to

100g" directive and matches every other price surface, but it's a visible change
to a number you may have been reading as /kg — say if you'd rather the breakdown

## 2026-09-13 — **Templates redesigned, and the desktop/mobile audit the owner asked for**

**Status: built and gated, NOT driven in the browser.** pytest **2384 passed**
(the four known FU-762 reds only), vitest **737 / 65 files**, `vue-tsc`,
`eslint src/`, `quasar build` clean. **`MealPlanTemplatesDrawer.vue` deleted**,
**`MealPlanApplyTemplateDialog.vue` added**. Reverses **FU-308** deliberately.

**Templates.** Owner: *"the presentation and usage of templates here is genuinely
terrible and a little confusing. Redo it."* The diagnosis was that one side
sheet, reached from a menu item called *"Apply template…"*, did four unrelated
jobs — saved the current week (a duplicate of the overflow item that opened it),
applied recurring **through a second modal stacked on the sheet**, renamed and
deleted each row, and linked out to the sets page. Applying was one button among
them. Rebuilt to the owner's own layout:
- **`MealPlanApplyTemplateDialog`** — a radio list of templates (sets listed with
  them), a **Repeat for several weeks** toggle that reveals the range *inline*,
  one action button. Choosing a set forces repeat on and says why: rotating is
  what a set is, so it has no single-week meaning.
- **Toolbar** gains *Apply template* left of *Build my week* — two ways to fill
  an empty week in one move, so they sit together.
- **Overflow** keeps *Save week as template…* and gains *Manage templates…*.
- **The Templates page** grew a *Your templates* section (inline rename +
  delete) above the rotating sets, and its heading is now just "Templates".
- The page's standalone recurring dialog and its five refs are gone.

**This reverses FU-308 (2026-07-07) on purpose**, which had moved per-template
CRUD *into* the drawer on the reasoning that managing belongs beside applying.
In use that is what made the drawer four surfaces in one. The reversal is written
into the page itself, not left as a silent flip, and FU-308's one good idea (the
inline rename, over the old `$q.dialog.prompt`) is kept.

**The audit.** Owner: *"there might be some inconsistencies between desktop and
mobile. Find them and decide with me."* Two turned out to be by design and were
reported as such: past-day **collapsing** (the phone shows one day, so there is
nothing to fold) and the **All slots** toggle (the phone always sections every
slot). Five were real; the owner chose on three:
1. **No over-budget warning existed on a phone at all** — the panel rendered
   inside the desktop week scroller only. Now a `#alert` slot above the day
   strip, filled by the page with the same component: the panel stays page-owned
   (it holds the plan id and the reload), placement is the mobile view's.
2. **Week heading** — the phone had a plain bold label, no relative label and no
   planned count. Now the calendar's uppercase voice with the same split line.
3. **Apply template** was promoted on desktop, a menu item on the phone. Now a
   matched pair with Build my week — **owner amended my proposal**: side by side,
   equal width, not stacked.
4. **Per-day kcal** was desktop-only. Owner chose to **drop it from desktop**
   rather than add it to the phone, following the per-day cost total out on
   09-12 for the same reason. `dayNutrition` went with its only consumer.
5. **The phone's day header** read "Sunday 13 September" under a week range and a
   numbered day strip. Now "Sunday" — the same duplication that took the dates
   off the desktop day headers on 09-12.

**Also:** the budget line moved *inside* the cost card as "$62 remaining of $150
budget" (it was a caption below it, which read as a note about the rail rather
than the other half of the same question).

**Decisions made:**
- **The apply dialog owns no `t:`/`s:` encoding of its own** — it emits the same
  token `useMealPlanner.recurringSourceOptions` already uses, so the choice has
  one representation rather than two that can drift.
- **`day_nutrition` stays on the DTO.** Removing a server field because its
  current consumer went is a wider change than the owner asked for, and a future
  surface may want a day's calories. Only the client plumbing went.
- **The mobile alert is a slot, not a prop.** Passing `mealPlanId` down so the
  phone could mount its own copy would mean two instances fetching the same
  suggestions at different breakpoints.

`MealPlanShoppingSummary.vue`, `MealPlanMobileFocus.vue`, `MealPlanWeekDayCard.vue`,

**deleted** `MealPlanTemplatesDrawer.vue`. Docs: `CHANGELOG.md`, `DORA_VERIFY.md`.

## 2026-09-12 (fifth) — **Eleven more planner items: the banner deleted, the pips re-derived, and the middle pane put back on the app's type scale**

**Status: built and gated, NOT driven in the browser.** pytest **2384 passed**
(the four known FU-762 reds only), vitest **737 / 65 files**, `vue-tsc`,

**The two questions, answered:**
- *"Why is the route `monday=`?"* — it was the focused week's Monday, so the key
  was named after the **encoding** rather than the thing. Renamed to `?week=`
  outright (no compat alias — nothing is released, and `mondayOf()` already
  normalises whatever day the URL names, so a hand-typed mid-week date still
  resumes correctly).
- *"What does the calendar day pip show now?"* — it showed only the readiness
  half (`needs_cooking`), so after the card gained a second axis a day of meals
  you had no ingredients for was six green pips. `pipForEntry` now takes the
  card's own trim roll-up, so the month view and the week cards cannot disagree
  about which days are fine. It needed `batchEnabled` threaded through both
  callers, which is also what tells the shared rule whether the readiness axis
  exists at all for this household.

**The banner.** `MealPlanWeekStatus` is deleted at both breakpoints — owner:
*"it just repeats info readily available elsewhere."* It did: the shortfall and
to-buy cells restated the meal cards and the rail's own per-item counts, less
precisely. The two survivors moved to where they belong — the **planned count**
into the week scroller beside "in 2 weeks", the **week cost** into a small
non-collapsible **Cost this week** card under the rail's lists (a card, not a
disclosure: one figure has nothing to collapse), with its three-sentence InfoTip
cut to one line.

**Free-text ingredients became real rows.** The list landed an hour earlier as
name + recipe with an explanatory paragraph. It is now the same
`MealPlanIngredientRow` the other two lists draw: hover highlights the source
meals, and the caption carries the amount the week needs. That required the
server's `UnlinkedIngredientDto` to carry `recipe_id`, `quantity` and `unit` —
the first is what the planner highlights by, the second is what the other rows
put in their caption, and the quantity is scaled to planned servings so the two
lists quote the same week.

**Type scale.** Owner: *"everything is teeny tiny — compare with stock
overview."* It was measurably so: the meal chip's name was inherited body
(~0.875rem) in a 28px chip, where `StockItemRow` gives its name 1.05rem in 64px.
The chip's name is now `--font-size-md` on a 36px floor, the servings pill and
slot labels moved onto the token scale, the phone card's 0.72rem meta line went
to `--font-size-sm` with a 48px thumb, and the three status glyphs are 22px.

**The rest:** collapsed rail strip drops its count / the open header shows it as
the shared `MealPlanRailCount` badge · the week range wears the calendar's
uppercase tracked voice · **TODAY** capitalised at both breakpoints · "All
slots" moved up beside Build my week (row 1 has the width now the status row is
gone) · price sits immediately left of the three icons · the cookability tooltip
says **"Cookable now"**, the cookbook's own words for that state.

**Decisions made:**
- **The free-text adapter is explicit, not a second row component.** What
  differs is the *data* (no stock item ⇒ no level, no cart), not the layout, and
  the owner asked for the layout to be the same. `stock_item_id: ''` resolves
  through `useStockStatus` to no level and the row renders "Not tracked", which
  is the honest reading for an ingredient with nothing behind it.
- **`Cost this week` is money-gated, not hidden-when-empty.** With money off the

- **The pip keeps three states, not four.** A fourth ("can't cook it") would ask
  a 6px dot to carry an axis the tooltip and the card already separate; "this
  day needs you" is what a month view is for.

## 2026-09-12 (third) — **The meal card's signal vocabulary, rebuilt around one axis per channel**

**Status: built and gated, NOT driven in the browser.** pytest **2384 passed**
(the four known FU-762 reds only), vitest **735 / 65 files**, `vue-tsc`,
`eslint src/`, `quasar build` clean.

**The assessment that drove it.** The owner spotted that cookability and
shortfall were being signalled "using colours that mean the same thing and icons
that mean multiple things", and asked whether the green trim was carrying
anything at all. Inventorying the card confirmed both: **amber** meant *"the
pool is short, go cook this"*, *"you're missing ingredients, you can't cook
this"* and *"Dora thinks an ingredient ran out"* — three different instructions
— while **green** meant *cooked*, *Dora's good-news hunch*, and, on the trim of
every ordinary meal, **nothing**. An always-on signal carries no information;
wearing a verdict colour, it gets read as a verdict, which is why a leftovers
day looked like an all-clear beside an amber one.

Root cause: three independent axes (provenance · supply · labour) multiplexed
into two colour channels, assigned per feature as each one landed.

**The fix — one axis per channel** (`helpers/mealPlanEntryStatus.ts`, shared by
both cards):
- **Supply** — `chef_hat`, green/amber. Applies only where a meal is cooked
  from ingredients.
- **Readiness** — `mealsPrepared` (the fridge), green/amber. Batch households
  only, and never on a `cook_fresh` meal.
- **Trim** — a *roll-up* of the two, so it cannot contradict them: green all
  good, grey nothing-required (leftovers, consumed), amber if either glyph is.
- **Provenance** — chips, no verdict colour. `Cook day · 6 servings` /
  `Leftovers` / `Fresh`, plus the price.

An axis that doesn't apply renders **nothing** (owner call) rather than a greyed
glyph: a green chef hat on a leftovers day would claim a shop you never have to
do, and a fridge in a fresh household describes a store that doesn't exist.

**Also in this pass:**
- **`cook_batch_estimated_cost`** on the entry DTO — the sum of a batch's own
  per-entry figures, so the cook day's price chip and the week total can't
  drift. The cook day prices the whole cook; its leftover days price nothing,
  because the money is spent once (owner call).
- **Day cost rollups removed** from both the desktop day header and the phone
  day header (owner: *"too much text to look at, and we can see X/X priced based
  on presence of a price chip"*). The week total stays.
- **"Cook now" from a planned meal is guarded** — it pushed straight to cook
  mode, while the recipe page and the cookbook both ask first. Third consumer of
  `helpers/cookModeGuard`, which is exactly what that helper exists for.
- **"Pool" is gone from user-facing copy** — the meal menu's cook-fresh caption,
  the week status "fresh" tip, the dashboard's Next-to-cook empty state and the
  recipe page's free-meals tooltip all talk about **ready servings** now.
- **The builder's "N to buy" marker was cut** the same day it landed (owner:
  *"just noise in the builder"*); the aggregate below the rows already answers it
  for the whole proposal.
- Week-grid day names took the auto builder's day-divider voice.

**Decisions made:**
- **`shortfall` stayed the prop name** on both cards even though the copy no
  longer says it. It is the server's own concept (`needs_cooking` ← the pool
  allocation) and renaming the prop without renaming the field would put a
  second vocabulary between them. Flagged here rather than half-done.
- **The day name was NOT centred** in the week grid. Its header row also holds
  the collapse chevron, the date, a Today badge and the calorie cell; centring
  one item of five reads as misalignment, not as a heading. The auto builder's
  divider is centred because it owns its own line. Worth a look when walked.
- **`mealPlanEntryFlags.ts` was deleted, not extended.** It answered one
  boolean ("flag the gap?"); the card now needs three coordinated answers, and
  keeping the old helper beside the new one would leave two places deciding when
  a leftovers day speaks.

**Files touched:** `dora_api/features/meal_plans/get_meal_plans.py`;
`web_app/src/helpers/mealPlanEntryStatus.ts` (new, replaces
`mealPlanEntryFlags.ts`), `src/css/mealChips.scss` (new, registered in
`quasar.config.ts`), `MealPlanEntryChip.vue`, `MealPlanRichCard.vue`,
`MealPlanWeekDayCard.vue`, `MealPlanMobileFocus.vue`, `MealPlanBuilderDialog.vue`,
`MealPlanEntryMenu.vue`, `MealPlanWeekStatus.vue`, `MealPlansOverview.vue`,
`dashboard/NextToCookCard.vue`, `RecipeDetailPage.vue`, `src/models/mealPlan.ts`.
Tests: `test/unit/mealPlanEntryStatus.spec.ts` (new, 14 cases),
`mealPlanEntryKey.spec.ts`. Docs: `CHANGELOG.md`, `DORA_VERIFY.md`.

**Standards close-gate:** R-001 — the two cards share the status rule and the
chip stylesheet rather than each owning a copy. R-003 — the price chip does no
money arithmetic; the batch figure is server-summed. D-002 — warning colour
stays on glyphs, never on text ink. D-014 — every state still carries icon +
text (tooltip/aria), never colour alone. **Candidate ADR, not written:** "one
axis per channel; a signal that is always on is decoration" is a real recurring
rule and this is its second sighting (the stocktake belief copy earlier today
was the same class of defect — a channel saying something it didn't need to).
Left for the next UI unit to confirm as a pattern before promoting it to an
R-rule, rather than minting one off a single day.

**Next up:** owner walks the new DORA_VERIFY section — the two-glyph card and
the batch price chip are the two that most want eyes.

## 2026-09-12 (second) — **Meal-planner batch: ~20 owner items, three of them real bugs**

**Status: built and gated, NOT driven in the browser.** pytest **2384 passed**
(the four known FU-762 reds only), vitest **729 / 65 files**, `vue-tsc`,
`eslint src/`, `quasar build` clean. Opens **FU-907** and **FU-908**.

**Three decisions were the owner's, taken up front rather than guessed:**
1. **Budget cap basis — kept as-is, made transparent.** The alternative (count
   only what you'd have to buy) was offered and declined; what changed is that
   the review step now states the to-buy figure beside the meal-value one, so
   the number the cap works to is no longer the only number on screen.
2. **Cookable state — flag the gap only.** No positive state (Charter 10), no
   third colour competing with the batch-pool amber.
3. **Reshuffle — sample among the near-best and rotate the days.**

**The bugs (found by reading the code the questions pointed at):**
- **The builder priced the pot, not the plan.** `estimated_cost` per proposed
  entry was the recipe's whole yield — the step-1 servings control changed
  nothing, and a 3-day batch cook was counted **three times**. The budget cap
  was then swapping meals on that inflated figure. Now
  `cost_per_serving × entry servings`, which is exactly what
  `get_meal_plans._hydrate_cost` has always done for a saved week (R-003), so a
  batch's days sum to one cook. This is the answer to *"are linked meal slots
  accounted for properly?"* — they were not.
- **Reshuffle was out-voted, not broken.** The per-candidate jitter was ≤1.5
  against 2.0 for cookable and 3.0 per expiring ingredient, so only a pool of
  exactly-equal candidates (which the unit tests build and a kitchen doesn't)
  ever varied. Replaced with **sampling**: take the candidates within
  `NEAR_BEST_WINDOW` of the leader, cap at four, choose one — then shuffle the
  placement order so the days rotate too. No rng ⇒ plain argmax, so the fixture
  tests stay deterministic.
- **`.rich-card__status { margin-left: auto }`** pushed the status glyph to the
  right edge and dragged servings/time/cost with it — so only the meals *with* a
  glyph right-aligned, which is the *"green on the left, orange on the right"*
  report. One line.

**New server-owned data (both R-003, both replacing a client-side derivation):**
- `MealPlanIngredientsDto` gains **`low_count` / `out_count` / `to_buy_cost` /
  `meals_cost`** (`summarise_demand`). The bands are counted separately because
  *"we don't necessarily need to buy low items"*, and both figures come from
  `estimate_cost_for_ingredients` — the aggregate is shimmed through the recipe
  pricing ladder rather than estimated a second way. Money-gated. The builder
  stopped counting to-buy rows itself through `useStockStatus`.
- `MealPlanEntryDto` gains **`missing_count`** (`_hydrate_cookability` →
  `load_recipe_cookability`), so a week card can flag a meal you can't cook
  without the client re-deriving cookability against the stock store.

**The rest of the batch:** step 1 renamed **Setup**; the servings stepper in a
shrink-to-fit wrapper; the headcount sentence cut; "Dora will plan N meals"
moved into an info box above the action row; the review rows rebuilt as cards
(servings + delete on the name's line, no swap glyph, centred day divider in the
recipe page's `.rn__sectitle` voice); `picked` and `cookable_now` chips given
empty labels so they render nothing; "Cook once" → **Cook day**; leftovers grey;
the A-Z/Cheapest control moved into the chip row via a new `#trailing` slot; a
**Can cook now** chip (`cookable === true` only — the tri-state unknown is not
an invitation); "Any level" → "Any difficulty"; the desktop target line is a
tinted card and the phone sheet names the destination in its **title** instead,
dropping the Done button that did nothing there.

**Decisions made:**
- **`showsMissingIngredients` is a shared helper, not a computed in each card.**
  The chip and the rich card would otherwise each own a four-clause rule about
  batch households, and a drift between them is invisible until you open both
  breakpoints (R-001). It has its own spec.
- **The cookability hydrate is not gated on anything.** "Can I cook this" is the
  planner's core question, unlike money or nutrition. The cost of that is
  **FU-908** — an unbounded cookbook read per plan fetch — logged rather than
  hidden.
- **`meals_per_pick` on the budget cap is a uniform scalar**, so a short final
  batch chunk rounds up. Logged as **FU-907**; the honest fix is to apply the
  cap after placement, which is a restructure this batch didn't own.
- **`missing_count` for a manual add in the builder** is read from the
  cookbook's own recipe rather than from the proposal, because a client-built
  entry has no `missing_stock_item_names` — one lookup, same server field.

**Files touched:** `dora_api/features/meal_plans/build_week.py`,
`get_meal_plan_ingredients.py`, `get_meal_plans.py`;
`web_app/src/components/MealPlanBuilderDialog.vue`, `MealPlanRecipePicker.vue`,
`MealPlanRailFilterChips.vue`, `MealPlanPickerSheet.vue`, `MealPlanRichCard.vue`,
`MealPlanEntryChip.vue`, `src/helpers/recipeRailFilters.ts`,
`src/helpers/mealPlanEntryFlags.ts` (new), `src/models/mealPlan.ts`. Tests:
`tests/test_build_week.py` (+4), `tests/e2e/dora_api/test_meal_plan_preview.py`
(+1, +1 amended), `test/unit/mealPlanEntryFlags.spec.ts` (new),
`test/unit/recipeRailFilters.spec.ts` (+2), `test/unit/mealPlanEntryKey.spec.ts`.
Docs: `CHANGELOG.md`, `DORA_VERIFY.md`, `DORA_FOLLOWUPS.md`.

**Standards close-gate:** R-003 is the rule this unit applies twice (both new
server fields replace client-side derivation). R-001 honoured by extracting
`showsMissingIngredients` and by the chip row's slot rather than a second sort
control. R-058 honoured — both new figures are null with money off. D-002: the
new "N to buy" markers keep warning colour on the glyph and page ink on the
words. No ADR: nothing here is a new recurring decision.

**Next up:** owner walks `DORA_VERIFY.md`'s new meal-planner section; FU-907 /

## 2026-09-12 — **Stocktake belief copy: the band said once**

**Status: built and gated, NOT driven in the browser.** pytest **2379 passed**
(the four known FU-762 reds only), vitest **720 / 64 files**, `vue-tsc`,
`eslint src/` and `quasar build` clean. Five owner items, all copy/presentation;
no schema, no API shape change.

**What changed:**
- **`_cadence_reason` (`pantry_belief.py`) dropped its band prefix and its
  tildes.** It returned `"~Out — bought 26 days ago…"` and every surface that
  renders it already renders the band beside it (`PantryBeliefChip`,
  `PantryBeliefCard`, the overview row's level-picker menu header,
  and now the walk card), so the verdict was being stated twice. Now:
  `"Bought 26 days ago, cooked with 2× since; your usual 28-day supply should
  be gone."` Capitalised because the string also starts a standalone sentence
  in `suggestions/generators.py` and the buy verdict's need axis. Measured on
  three fixtures before/after rather than reasoned about.
- **Review phase** (`StocktakeReviewPhase.vue`): "— no need to go and look"
  cut; `· recorded as` → `· but is currently`; the recorded pill now speaks
  belief's vocabulary (`recordedWord` maps a level *sequence* → band word, so a
  household level named "Low Stock" reads **Low** beside "Dora thinks Low"),
  falling back to the catalogue name for any level off the three canonical
  sequences; the per-row reason line **removed** (and its dead style with it).
- **Walk card** (`StocktakeRunner.vue`): "Dora's not sure about this one — " is
  gone — it was on every card, and it's the premise of the runner, not news.
  The box now leads with a `Dora thinks <band>` head line in the chip's own
  words, reason underneath.

**Decisions made:**
- **Fixed server-side, not per-surface.** The reason is server-owned copy
  (R-003) precisely so one sentence appears everywhere; stripping the prefix in
  the two stocktake components would have left the same double-statement live
  on the overview picker and the item page, which is where the owner also saw
  it ("same issue ... from the overview dropdown picker").
- **The recorded pill falls back to the catalogue name** rather than forcing a
  band word. A household can add levels; there is no band word for a fourth
  one, and inventing one would be worse than the inconsistency being fixed.
- **The other belief reasons keep their em dashes** ("Based on the last
  recorded level … — not enough history to infer yet"). The owner's complaint
  named the cadence string's `~`/`—`; those dashes are doing ordinary
  sentence work, and R-003's one-voice rule cuts against churning copy that
  wasn't reported.

**Files touched:** `dora_api/features/stock_items/pantry_belief.py`,
`web_app/src/components/stocktake/StocktakeReviewPhase.vue`,
`web_app/src/pages/StocktakeRunner.vue`. Docs: `CHANGELOG.md`, `DORA_VERIFY.md`
(three new checks; the 09-01 dark-theme item reworded off the deleted string).

**Standards close-gate:** no R-rule violations introduced. R-003 is the rule
this unit *applies* (one owner for the belief sentence). D-001 colour roles

## 2026-09-09 (fourth) — **FU-904 + FU-905, and the level chip reverted to 32px**

**Status: built and gated, NOT driven in the browser.** pytest **2372 passed**
(the four known FU-762 reds only), vitest **720 / 64 files**, `vue-tsc`,
`eslint src/`, `quasar build` clean. **Resolves FU-904 and FU-905.**

**What changed:**
- **New `features/nutrition/household_measures.py`** — the pure grams
  resolution (`resolve_grams`, `match_portion`, `grams_from_portion`,
  `COUNT_MEASURE_PREFERENCE`) plus the two batched loaders, extracted from
  `recipe_rollup` and now called by both calculators. It states the precedence
  once: **a measured portion row beats a modelled density.** That alone settles
  FU-905's second half — a cup of plain flour was 125 g on the nutrition panel
  and 132.5 g in the cost breakdown, and is now 125 on both.
- **Costing can weigh things.** `portions_by_stock_item()` (two batched queries
  per entry point) feeds a `by_weight()` route in `_line_cost`, used when the
  price is per mass. "2 leeks" against $6.90/kg is **$1.23** instead of
  unpriced; "1 cup frozen peas" **$0.58**; "2 sticks celery" **$0.32** — the
  right answer at last, after being $0.90 (butter) and then unpriced.
- **`units.SUB_ITEM_UNITS`** — twelve words that name a *part* of a shelf item
  (`clove`, `sprig`, `rasher`, `slice`, `stalk`, `floret`, `leaf`, `wedge`) or
  a vague amount with no size (`knob`, `splash`, `drizzle`, `handful`).
  `_line_cost` never counts one as a whole product. **3 cloves of garlic: $3.60
  → unpriced**, or **$0.06** when a portion row knows a clove is 3 g.
- **The stock level chip is back to 32px on touch.** The 09-05 sweep read the
  owner's *"bit thicker/bigger for mobile"* as being about the button; it was
  about the **rows in the menu it opens**, which are 44px and stay that way
  (`app.scss`), beside the 200→260px menu widening. Reverted with the reasoning
  kept in place as an R-085/D-004 carve-out.

**Measured on the same 18-ingredient pie** (before this unit → after):

| line | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `2 whole` Leeks @ $6.90/kg | unpriced | **$1.23** |
| `1 cup` Frozen Peas @ $4.30/kg | unpriced | **$0.58** |
| `2 sticks` Celery @ $4/kg | unpriced | **$0.32** |
| `3 cloves` Garlic @ $1.20/bulb | **$3.60** | unpriced |
| `2 sprigs` Tarragon @ $2.50/bunch | **$5.00** | unpriced |
| `0.25 cup` Plain Flour | $0.06 (33.1 g, density) | $0.06 (**31.25 g**, portion row) |

Priced 11/18 either way, but the composition changed: three lines that were
silently wrong left, three that were honestly missing arrived. Cost and grams
now agree on every line where both resolve.

**Decisions made:**
- **`portions_by_stock_item` is deliberately NOT gated on the nutrition mode.**
  Those rows exist because a dataset was imported and foods were linked, which
  is true whether or not nutrition is currently set to complex. Gating would
  mean a household's grocery estimate silently improving because someone
  flipped a nutrition setting — a stranger coupling than reading data that is
  simply present. R-058 is about not *computing* money features when money is
  off, which both callers still honour. No dataset ⇒ `{}` ⇒ every path falls
  back to exactly the old behaviour, pinned by its own test.
- **Sub-item words prefer weight over refusal.** Refusing "3 cloves" outright
  was the option in the FU; routing it through `by_weight()` first means the
  common case (a portion row for `clove`, a per-kilo garlic price) gets a real
  number rather than a gap. Refusal is the fallback, not the rule.
- **`head` and `bunch` are not on the list**, though they look like they
  belong: a head of garlic and a bunch of coriander *are* the things you buy,
  so counting them is correct.
- **The level chip's carve-out is written down rather than silently reverted.**
  It is the one place in the tap-target sweep where D-004's floor cost
  something real — the chip is a colour block, so hit area *is* visual weight —
  and the usual escape (hold the size, grow the target with a pseudo-element)
  is unavailable because `::after` carries the uncertainty ring and QBtn owns
  `::before`. The comment names the trade so the next sweep doesn't re-apply it.
- **`_foods_by_id` stayed in `recipe_rollup`.** Nutrient figures are that
  module's business; only the portion rows beside them answer a question
  costing also asks.

**Files touched:** `dora_api/features/nutrition/household_measures.py` (new),
`dora_api/features/nutrition/recipe_rollup.py` (delegates; ~90 lines removed),
`dora_api/features/recipes/recipe_cost.py`, `dora_api/domain/units.py`,
`web_app/src/components/stock/StockLevelPicker.vue`. Tests:
`tests/test_recipe_line_cost.py` (13 → 23 cases). Docs: `CHANGELOG.md`,
`DORA_VERIFY.md`, `DORA_FOLLOWUPS.md` (FU-902 amended),
`DORA_FOLLOWUPS_RESOLVED.md` (FU-904, FU-905).

**Verification:**
- The pie harness re-run after every step; the table above is its output, not a
  reading of the diff. Deleted after use.
- `test_recipes_query_count` is a **ratio** test, so the two new batched
  queries per entry point are safe by construction — and they are batched over
  the whole page, so the per-recipe delta is unchanged. Confirmed green.
- **Not verified:** none of it in a running browser, including the level chip's
  size on a real phone — which is the one thing here that only glass can settle.

**Next up:**
1. Owner walks the `DORA_VERIFY.md` cost items and confirms the level chip
   reads right again at 32px.
2. **FU-875** (splitting the vague "units don't match the price" message) is
   now the natural next one — its blocker is gone and this unit added a fourth
   situation the bucket conflates.

**Open questions for user:**
- Anything else that should be on `SUB_ITEM_UNITS`? It is deliberately short.
  Candidates I left off as too ambiguous: `piece`, `fillet`, `stick` (already
  handled separately), `bunch`, `head`.
